newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies U.S. charges it violates Iraq sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies U.S. charges it violates Iraq sanctions.

text.p: Iran rejected on Tuesday U.S. accusations that Tehran violated United Nations sanctions on Iraq by allowing Iraqi gasoil to be smuggled through Iranian waters, the official news agency IRNA said.
It quoted a statement by the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) as saying: "Iran has never ignored the U.N. embargo on Iraq in the past nor will it do so in the future."

The statement came in reaction to a briefing last week by U.S. naval commanders to the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq which alleged that increasing amounts of Iraqi gasoil were being smuggled through Iranian waters.
"The statement said the NIOC's regulations on exchange of oil and using terminals for crude oil and oil derivatives in the Persian Gulf are crystal clear to international observers," IRNA reported.
"As before, all false rumours being spread by American officials are totally unfounded," the company said.
Iraq has been under stringent U.N. sanctions since it invaded Kuwait in 1990. A U.S.-led force drove Baghdad's forces out in 1991.
